questions.question: At 90 Hz, what is the approximate frame interval?
questions.explanation: The interval is 1000 / 90, or about 11.1 milliseconds.

questions.question: Why is a frame interval not a universal motion-to-photon guarantee?
options: The full path also includes sensing, tracking, rendering, composition, display, and possible transport
questions.explanation: The frame interval is one planning unit; the observed end-to-end path contains several measured stages.

questions.question: Which responsibility should remain local when rendering moves to an edge service?
questions.explanation: Local pose, boundaries, input, and exit behavior should not depend on remote frame delivery.

questions.question: Remote frame delivery starts jittering while local tracking is valid. What should degrade first?
questions.explanation: Reducing remote detail preserves the trustworthy local control loop.

questions.question: What should happen when world-relative tracking is lost?
options: Continue world-locked interactions from the last pose
Pause placement-sensitive actions and expose recovery
questions.explanation: World-locked behavior is unsafe when the runtime cannot provide a trustworthy pose.

questions.question: Why does a shared anchor need a mapping epoch?
options: To identify the coordinate-frame version behind its pose
questions.explanation: Coordinates from conflicting mapping epochs cannot be merged safely without reconciliation.

questions.question: Which test best exposes a remote-rendering recovery flaw?
options: Injected jitter, loss, saturation, and out-of-order frames while the user moves
questions.explanation: Movement plus transport and capacity faults exercises the timing and fallback contract.
